title: const with pointers: pointer-to-const and const-pointer (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C language rules.
Trace the example and explain data flow.
Identify common errors and boundary conditions.
Apply the concept in a small tested program.

understand.concept: const qualifies the type of an object or the type accessed through a pointer. A pointer to const int prevents modification through that pointer; a const pointer prevents changing the pointer value after initialization. Both qualifiers can be combined.
understand.whyItMatters: Reading declarations from the identifier outward helps distinguish whether the pointed-to value, the pointer itself or both are restricted.
understand.analogy: Treat a function or pointer operation as an explicit contract between caller and callee.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal rules for types, object lifetime, scope and linkage.

explain.narrative:
const qualifies the type of an object or the type accessed through a pointer. A pointer to const int prevents modification through that pointer; a const pointer prevents changing the pointer value after initialization. Both qualifiers can be combined.

When applying this concept, check declared types, preconditions, object lifetime and all control-flow paths. Compile with warnings enabled and test both typical and boundary inputs.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: read_only may be redirected but cannot modify score through that pointer. fixed_address cannot be redirected after initialization, but it can modify score because its pointed-to type is int.

practise.guidedTask: For each declaration, state whether the pointer can move and whether the object can be modified through it.
practise.independentTask: Write a function that receives a read-only array using a pointer-to-const parameter.
hints: const int *p and int const *p both mean pointer to const int.
const on a pointer parameter does not make the caller's separate pointer variable const.
Do not cast away const and modify an object that was originally defined as const.
